findings.description: If `os.fdopen` fails, `fd` is never closed. If `os.replace` succeeds and the exception is raised later (e.g. KeyboardInterrupt), or the temp file is already gone, `os.unlink(tmp_name)` raises FileNotFoundError and replaces the original exception. A bare `except:` also catches BaseException, which is too broad here.
findings.suggestion: Use `except BaseException:` with `contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError)` around the unlink, or a try/finally that removes the temp file only if it still exists; close the fd if fdopen fails.
findings.title: Bare except cleanup can mask the original error and leak the temp file

findings.description: The old `get` deleted expired sessions on access. The new one only returns None, and nothing else calls `purge_expired`. Expired sessions stay in memory and, in FileSessionStore, are rewritten to disk on every commit, so the store and file grow without bound unless a caller purges regularly.
findings.suggestion: Either document and schedule `purge_expired`, or purge expired entries inside `create`, which already takes the write lock.
findings.title: Expired sessions are no longer removed on get, so they accumulate until purge_expired is called

findings.description: `_load` only handles FileNotFoundError. Invalid JSON, a missing key or a malformed timestamp raises JSONDecodeError, KeyError or ValueError from the constructor, so the application cannot start until the file is removed by hand.
findings.suggestion: Catch decode errors in `_load`, log them, and start with an empty store (or move the bad file aside).
findings.title: A corrupt or partially written session file crashes startup
